subject: MAP: Evaluation window compression & cutover readiness
messages:
From: Elaine Porter <elaine.porter@novahealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@novahealth.com, Tom Hargreaves <tom.hargreaves@novahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP update — potential acceptance window compression

Hi Kimberly,

Quick heads-up: our internal security review flagged two outstanding evidence items for SOC2 (log retention & third-party access attestations). The security team is asking for the evidence pack by EOD Wednesday to keep the current go‑live window.

At the moment that looks tight for us — procurement is pushing for the current close date to stick, but security is firm on their gating checklist. Can you share the latest MAP with clear milestone owners and a proposed contingency if we need to shorten the evaluation window by 3 business days?

We want to avoid moving the public cutover but need to surface the risk and an executable fallback if there is slippage.

Thanks,
Elaine
Elaine Porter
VP, Product Delivery
Nova Health Systems

[Attachment: none]

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Porter <elaine.porter@novahealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Jan 2028 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP update — potential acceptance window compression

Elaine — thanks for the note and for pulling the ask forward. Short answer: we can support a compressed evaluation but need to make the tradeoffs explicit.

Immediate actions I propose:
- I will circulate an updated MAP with compressed evaluation scenarios (3-day and 5-day compression) and clear owner actions by tomorrow COB.
- Marcus (SE) will outline the reduced-scope validation checklist we can run in parallel to your security team's review.
- Ben (AE) will align procurement on the revised acceptance milestone language so there are no surprises at contract sign.

Two quick clarifying Qs from my side:
1) Which exact evidence items are blocking you (security mentioned log retention & third-party access, are there others)?
2) Is there any internal decision date (exec signoff) we should preserve for your board reporting?

I’ll send the MAP v3 with attachments tomorrow — flagging for internal follow-up.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Director, GTM Ops
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: none]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, Elaine Porter <elaine.porter@novahealth.com>, Tom Hargreaves <tom.hargreaves@novahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jan 2028 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed MAP v3 and reduced validation checklist

Kimberly / Elaine / Tom — attaching the proposed MAP v3. Highlights:

- Scenario A: 3-day evaluation compression — recommended when security can accept an interim log-sampling audit (owners: Nova Security / Redwood SE).
- Scenario B: 5-day compression — requires temporary extension of support hours and a targeted QA sprint (owners: Redwood QA / Nova Ops).
- Each scenario includes a minimal acceptance checklist (3 items) for a fast smoke validation and an explicit rollback trigger (data migration stalled, >2 critical defects).

Attachment: Proposed_MAP_v3.pdf (see top of doc for the compressed-schedule table).

If Elaine confirms the minimal evidence list (log retention sample, access matrix export, and third-party subprocessor attestation), we can lock Scenario A and produce the smoke validation runbook by EOD Thursday.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

[Attachment stub: Proposed_MAP_v3.pdf (pdf, 780KB) — contains scenario table, milestone owners, smoke validation runbook]

From: Elaine Porter <elaine.porter@novahealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Hargreaves <tom.hargreaves@novahealth.com>, procurement@novahealth.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 11:55:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed MAP v3 and reduced validation checklist

Thanks Marcus — reviewed and useful. Two clarifications from my security lead:

1) Log retention: they will accept a 14-day sample in lieu of full policy proof if the export mechanism and retention policy are demonstrated during the smoke validation.
2) Third-party attestation: we need a named subprocessor list and the latest vendor agreements; procurement said they can surface the contracts but we need a Redwood point person to confirm no additional subprocessors are present.

Procurement also asked whether any of the compressed scenarios would change licensing or invoice triggers — they prefer any changes to be explicit in the SOW amendment.

Given these asks, the team is comfortable proceeding with Scenario A only if Redwood can deliver the smoke validation runbook and the subprocessor confirmation by Friday EOD. Otherwise, we must request a one-week push to the public cutover for our compliance committee to re-evaluate.

Elaine

On Thu, Jan 18, 2028 at 09:20 Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Adding the runbook checklist in the attachment (lightweight).
>
[Quoted message ends]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Porter <elaine.porter@novahealth.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, procurement@novahealth.com
Date: Fri, 19 Jan 2028 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Escalation / Exec note: decision matrix & requested deliverables

Elaine — appreciate the clarity. We're treating this as an operational escalation to ensure the go‑live does not slip without explicit agreement.

What Redwood will commit to by Friday EOD (our deliverables):
- Final smoke validation runbook (owner: Marcus)
- Formal subprocessor declaration & latest vendor list (owner: Legal with support from Marcus)
- SOW amendment draft that calls out acceptance criteria for the compressed Scenario A (owner: Ben / Contracts)

I've attached a short tabulated QA tracker your procurement team can use to sign off each item as it completes. If any item is incomplete by Friday 17:00 PST, we acknowledge Nova's right to request a one‑week deferral; we will prioritize resources to avoid that outcome.

Attachment: Nova_Security_QA.xlsx (tracker).

Looping in execs on both sides is OK if you want a once-off alignment call — we can do a 30-minute sync tomorrow morning to run the decision matrix.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[Attachment stub: Nova_Security_QA.xlsx (xlsx, 45KB)]

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Porter <elaine.porter@novahealth.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 20 Jan 2028 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: MAP alignment — executive summary & next steps

Team — summary and proposed next steps as requested: 

1) What Redwood will deliver by Fri 2028-01-19 17:00 PST:
   - Smoke validation runbook (Marcus)
   - Named subprocessor list + confirmation (Legal / Marcus)
   - Draft SOW amendment (Ben)

2) If all three items are complete and procurement signs the QA tracker, we will execute the compressed Scenario A (3-day evaluation compression) with acceptance criteria described in Proposed_MAP_v3.pdf. No license or invoice triggers change — SOW amendment will make that explicit.

3) If any item is incomplete at the deadline, Nova may request a one-week push to the public cutover. To keep momentum, Redwood suggests a daily 15-minute stand from Wed–Fri (12:30–12:45 PST) for status and rapid unblock. Invite sent.

4) Exec alignment: Ben offered a 30-minute call tomorrow AM. If your execs prefer to skip, please confirm in writing.

Action items: Elaine to confirm whether security accepts the 14-day log sample (yes/no). Nova procurement to confirm whether they want the SOW amendment to be reciprocal or unilateral.

Thanks all — we’ll treat this as highest priority and I’ll personally monitor progress.

—Kimberly Park
Senior Director, GTM Ops
Redwood Inference

[Links: HubSpot deal RDW-2028-009, docusign link for SOW amendment]
